title: Pronoun and possessive-determiner agreement
subtitle: Form, Structure, and Sense · 25 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **25 of the official questions in Form, Structure, and Sense are this one** — 13 Easy, 5 Medium, 7 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The blank is a single pronoun and the choices are pronouns that differ in number or person, like 'it/they/them/this/that/she', or possessive determiners mixed with contractions that sound the same, like 'its/it's/their/they're'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Go back and find the noun the blank refers to.
- It is often a sentence or more earlier, or it is the subject of the main clause that comes after an introductory phrase.
- 2) Decide whether it is singular or plural, and whether it is a person or a thing.
- 3) If a possessive is needed, rule out 'it's' and 'they're' because they mean 'it is' and 'they are', then choose the determiner whose number matches.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: A distracting noun of the other number sits closer to the blank than the real antecedent does, or a human-sounding pronoun is offered for a non-human antecedent.
The possessive versions also offer a contraction that sounds right when you read it aloud.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
A distracting noun of the other number sits closer to the blank than the real antecedent does, or a human-sounding pronoun is offered for a non-human antecedent.
The possessive versions also offer a contraction that sounds right when you read it aloud.
